- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at 10–15% below true peak.
- When sentiment is neutral or trending sideways, model exhibits mean reversion bias — forecast tends to be too low; add 1–3% to early forecast values.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true price by 1–4% in the first 7–10 days; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive positive sentiment), model may lag; add 1–3% to forecast 3–5 days ahead to capture momentum.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–7 days to reflect sentiment shift.
